_about: Every idea explored for the Earth House-Kit, with pros, cons and a verdict. Rendered to IDEAS_MATRIX.md by ideas_matrix.py. Verdicts: winner = in the lead design; adopt = in the kit as a supporting part; test = promising, waiting on a measurement; fallback = proven backup; niche = only for certain sites or uses; killed = failed its numbers (see GRAVEYARD.md).

ideas.idea: Fire site clay into small units (~1,000 °C)
ideas.pros: 0.9–3.0 MJ/kg from farm waste; 36–46 MPa typical brick; a century of Malvern practice; doesn't rot, burn or rust
ideas.cons: needs a kiln and fuel; 5–8% total shrinkage; each clay bed must be tested

ideas.idea: Compacted earth tilt-up panels (the original project)
ideas.pros: no firing; tilt-up lift checks out (3.0–5.7× with rebar)
ideas.cons: not rock: 0.3–1 MPa; 6 in + steel; ~900 kg panels; 7–28 day cure

ideas.idea: Melt the soil into rock (vitrification, cast basalt, microwave)
ideas.cons: 6–12 MWh per house; ~3.5 MW power; big melts cool for 1–2 years

ideas.idea: Fire the whole house in place (Geltaftan)
ideas.cons: tried in Iran and abandoned: fuel cost, pollution, uneven firing

ideas.idea: Fire the whole wall, or only its binder, in place
ideas.cons: ~12,600 kWh per house; heats a whole wall to fire 15% of it; shrinkage cracking

ideas.idea: Geopolymer (soil + fired clay + activator)
ideas.pros: actually uses the clay; no cement
ideas.cons: 0.3–0.7 t caustic activator per house; ~665 kg panels; handling hazards

ideas.idea: Concrete from screened sand and gravel
ideas.cons: 1.1–1.5 t cement per house; fails on clay fines (1.5–3.4 MPa)

ideas.idea: Lime-sand steam-cured blocks
ideas.cons: sandy sites only; 1.1–2.0 t lime; heavy 6.5 in walls

ideas.idea: Sulfur concrete walls
ideas.cons: melts at 115–120 °C and burns to SO₂; can't take swelling clay

ideas.idea: Bio-cemented sandstone (MICP/EICP)
ideas.cons: sand only; ~1 kg ammonium chloride waste per kg calcite; 2–6 t reagents per house

ideas.idea: Single-piece fired ceramic wall panel
ideas.pros: 3 in wall, no joints, no steel
ideas.cons: thick site-clay slabs very likely crack in a field kiln; industry only does 6–20 mm pressed slabs

ideas.idea: Solid fired brick laid on site
ideas.cons: 7.5 in walls, 16–18 t; slow wet trade; mortar

ideas.idea: Cellular unit: staggered 6-row webs, husk-filled
ideas.pros: U 0.62 and 9 h lag at 8 in; 6–8 mm webs dry in hours; ~32–40% clay
ideas.cons: thin webs must survive handling and grinding; impact untested

ideas.idea: Straight-through, diamond or truss web patterns
ideas.cons: each web is a heat highway: U 0.76–1.75

ideas.idea: Extrude the bulk through a die
ideas.pros: fast, uniform, the brick industry's method; one die for all dome voussoirs
ideas.cons: a die per cross-section; fixed shapes

ideas.idea: 3D-print clay units (bead-built ribs)
ideas.pros: any shape; less clay; custom corners, keys and one-offs
ideas.cons: slow; warping and layer-line cracking unknown

ideas.idea: Graded units: glass-cullet skin, husk-pored core, dense rims
ideas.pros: 8 in U ≈ 0.42; engobes cut absorption 14.8% → 3.2%; bone-like logic
ideas.cons: zones must shrink together; co-extrusion not yet tried

ideas.idea: Grind bed faces flat after firing
ideas.pros: ±0.5 mm, ≤0.2 mm flat makes mortarless work (Poroton Dryfix)
ideas.cons: a grinder station and dust control

ideas.idea: Husk ash as a flux for a glassy skin
ideas.cons: 90–97% silica: refractory at 1,000 °C and makes cristobalite

ideas.idea: Salt-glazed units
ideas.cons: needs 1,250–1,300 °C; releases HCl

ideas.idea: Dry-stacked panels clamped by 2 rods, tilted up
ideas.pros: ~282–413 kg panels; no cure wait; rods carry 11.7–18.8× the lift if joints open; demountable
ideas.cons: joints must stay tight (20–35% prestress loss assumed); untested at full size

ideas.idea: Grouted panels with bars
ideas.pros: stronger; the proven path for storm walls
ideas.cons: 5–28 day cure; not demountable

ideas.idea: On-site brick building (laying units by hand)
ideas.cons: slower than panels; more site labour

ideas.idea: Openings as module-wide gaps with sill and lintel panels
ideas.pros: never cut a panel; short lintels (Inca logic)
ideas.cons: window sizes follow the module

ideas.idea: Carbon steel set tight in the masonry
ideas.cons: rust expands and splits it (the Acropolis's 20th-century repairs)

ideas.idea: Japanese joinery rules: clay only presses; wedges and rods lock
ideas.pros: no mortar, no glue; every joint re-driven or opened
ideas.cons: precision required; steel wedges and rods still bought

ideas.idea: Wedged fired key blocks at the polygon folds (shachi-sen)
ideas.pros: draws panels together with spare travel to re-drive
ideas.cons: untested

ideas.idea: Clay hooks or tabs that carry tension
ideas.cons: fired clay is weak in tension; Greek masons used separate cramps for this reason

ideas.idea: Keystone ring: slide in from outside, hook the notch below, lock to a neighbour, pinned key last
ideas.pros: can't be pushed through; one assembly order; last piece is the lock
ideas.cons: every unit numbered; one broken unit holds up the course

ideas.idea: Guastavino/timbrel 'no formwork' vaulting
ideas.cons: works only because gypsum glues each tile; dry units have none

ideas.idea: 16–20-sided round plan
ideas.pros: 26% more floor per panel than a square; half the wind drag; self-bracing
ideas.cons: curved furniture walls; the 20-gon's dome margins are thin without ribs

ideas.idea: Square or box plan
ideas.cons: corner suction zones; Cd 1.2–1.4; needs bracing

ideas.idea: Clusters of domes around courtyards (a 5k ft² 'mansion')
ideas.pros: big homes from proven small spans; grow one dome at a time (Elemental)
ideas.cons: more wall per floor; links and gutters between domes

ideas.idea: One huge single span
ideas.cons: the 24-gon hall passes at GSF 2.2 but big spans eat margin fast

ideas.idea: Owners extend a closed dome ad hoc
ideas.cons: Iquique's fires and flimsy add-ons

ideas.idea: Ribbed dome: post-tensioned 16 in ribs + 6 in graded webs
ideas.pros: 35% less clay; rib GSF 4.2 (16-gon), 2.9 (20-gon); passes wind, snow, quake
ideas.cons: stainless tendons to buy and re-check; a central mast to build it

ideas.idea: Solid 16 in cellular voussoir dome to 51.8°
ideas.pros: all compression; one die; GSF 1.62 in wind (16-gon)
ideas.cons: heavier; 20-gon margins only 1.29–1.31

ideas.idea: 12 in dome voussoirs
ideas.cons: no thrust line fits in 50 m/s wind; joints slide

ideas.idea: Plain (unstressed) dry ribs
ideas.cons: GSF ~1.2 in wind; joints slide

ideas.idea: Full hemisphere
ideas.cons: hoop tension beyond 51.8° cracks the meridians (Pantheon, St Peter's)

ideas.idea: Seat-step voussoirs + closing keys, course by course
ideas.pros: builds without formwork or mortar; only compression on the clay
ideas.cons: slow hand-setting; a cord guide per unit

ideas.idea: Cocciopesto skin under overlapping fired scale tiles
ideas.pros: Roman 2,000-year record; its weight is what makes the dome pass wind
ideas.cons: limewash every 1–3 years

ideas.idea: Hung, interlocking fired siding over a vented cavity
ideas.pros: ~60% less solar gain; each board lifts out; lock uses only 2–5% of strength
ideas.cons: battens and hangers to buy; more parts

ideas.idea: Siding hung on nibs alone
ideas.cons: BS 5534 won't accept nibs against wind suction

ideas.idea: Fluted drainage bricks on a crowned compacted-earth pad
ideas.pros: moves roof water to a cistern and away from walls (Machu Picchu logic)
ideas.cons: pad compaction and PI testing on site

ideas.idea: A 'hydrophobic' fired face as the rain barrier
ideas.cons: fired ceramic is hydrophilic; beading needs siloxane that lasts 10–15 years

ideas.idea: Spray coatings (carbon-fibre epoxy, polyurea, elastomerics)
ideas.cons: trap vapour and salts; hide cracks; 7–20 year recoats; none pass ICC 500 on masonry

ideas.idea: Silicate mineral paint; light engobed tiles
ideas.cons: colour choices limited

ideas.idea: Siloxane repellent on the plinth only
ideas.cons: never on siding, dome or interiors

ideas.idea: Lime textile-reinforced mortar
ideas.cons: a repair, not a default

ideas.idea: Earth tubes, evaporative cooling or night flushing in Arkansas
ideas.cons: humid air: mould in tubes; evaporative cooling collapses at 80–90% RH

ideas.idea: Round drum + cap under 30°
ideas.pros: no corners; peak suction 9.4 kPa; roof takes only the 67 mph missile; dome coefficients exist
ideas.cons: 44 kN uplift to tie down

ideas.idea: Pyramid or steep cone that 'deflects' debris
ideas.cons: ICC 500 fires the missile perpendicular; faces ≥30° take the full 100 mph; no ASCE 7 coefficients

ideas.idea: Box with flat roof
ideas.cons: 21.8 kPa corner suction; 64 kN tie-down

ideas.idea: Sacrificial fired skin + cavity + grouted cellular core
ideas.pros: copies walls that already passed 100 mph
ideas.cons: grout cure; needs lab testing ($75–175k)

ideas.idea: Dry-stacked or sand-filled clay alone as a shelter wall
ideas.cons: 4 in solid brick shattered at ~76 mph

ideas.idea: Hemp-lime or husk-lime blocks for interior walls
ideas.pros: MBV 2–3.3; carbon store; quiet; code-listed as infill (IRC BL)
ideas.cons: 0.15–0.4 MPa (non-load-bearing); 6–10 weeks to dry

ideas.idea: Bio-lime infill in outer walls behind the siding
ideas.cons: not for the shelter core; weather and missile untested

ideas.idea: Hempcrete cast in the shell
ideas.cons: cast-in, not removable; a second wall system

ideas.idea: Hemp shiv briquettes as kiln fuel
ideas.cons: needs a supply

ideas.idea: Hemp cover crop on worked-out pit benches
ideas.pros: builds soil; ~13 t/ha reported on mine soil
ideas.cons: dislikes wet compacted acid clay; licence needed

ideas.idea: Treated whole bamboo: roof framing, posts, verandahs under cover
ideas.cons: borates are reproductive toxins; must stay covered and replaceable

ideas.idea: Feed bamboo at death, mineralize inside, plasma + silicate 'ionized dip'
ideas.pros: lab: silica + silane cut absorption 84.5%, MOE +15%
ideas.cons: frontier on whole culms; toughness rarely measured

ideas.idea: Bamboo in place of steel rods or tendons
ideas.cons: ~1/13 the stiffness of steel; creeps; can't hold prestress

ideas.idea: Ceramized bamboo (SiC) or silicon-fed living bamboo
ideas.cons: SiC needs >1,400 °C and is brittle; no evidence Si feeding helps

ideas.idea: Mycelium or bacteria for self-healing structure
ideas.cons: no mortar joints to heal; puts organisms and water in dry walls

ideas.idea: Mycelium interior acoustic panels
ideas.cons: weak, absorbs water, combustible

ideas.idea: Fibre-lined kiln fired by a husk gasifier
ideas.pros: near-free fuel; ~80% less soot than old kilns; flue heat dries ware
ideas.cons: firing control to learn

ideas.idea: Separate husk-ash burner at 600–700 °C
ideas.pros: makes reactive ash (the pozzolan) instead of cristobalite; waste heat to the dryer
ideas.cons: XRD testing every batch; a silica dust hazard

ideas.idea: Solar + battery runs the build, then the homes
ideas.cons: capital; battery kept cool

ideas.idea: 'The fired wall powers the house'
ideas.cons: firing energy is spent as heat; a wall stores nothing recoverable

ideas.idea: River sand-bar harvesting on the Ouachita
ideas.cons: ~98% of the watershed is dammed; downstream bed incision; 404/401/ESA permits

ideas.idea: Wilcox pit sand + grog from kiln rejects + Jones Mill quarry sand
ideas.cons: haul distance for quarry sand

ideas.idea: A factory where clay meets rice husks (Malvern), shipping kits by truckload
ideas.pros: costs mostly fixed; price scales with tonnes and trucks; lean shells ~$20–25/ft²
ideas.cons: real costs and scrap unknown until a pilot runs

ideas.idea: Storm shelter as the first certified product
ideas.pros: one clear standard; public funding; plays to heavy clay
ideas.cons: $75–175k and 12–18 months to certify

ideas.idea: Own daylight robotics (gantry stacking, pre-assembly)
ideas.pros: labour from 11.8 to 1.9 h/t; runs on solar hours
ideas.cons: $125–420k; pays back only at volume

ideas.idea: Start tiny, grow on grants (NSF SBIR, EPA, USDA)
ideas.pros: capital-light; each stage proves the next
ideas.cons: grant timing; don't build the plan on one grant

ideas.idea: Open-method charity instead of a company (early view)
ideas.cons: superseded once the factory-and-kit model gave a real price edge

ideas.idea: Arkansas residential safe-room rebates as first funding
ideas.cons: Arkansas's program ended in 2016; FEMA money there goes to community safe rooms

ideas.idea: Build 50 machines before one finished house
ideas.cons: Open Source Ecology's scope creep
